# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 40 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 40 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_040_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

This chapter contains one of Hermas's most theologically significant teachings: the doctrine of "second repentance." The question arises from a rigorist position — apparently some teachers held that baptismal forgiveness was absolute and post-baptismal sin was unforgivable. Hermas steers a middle path: post-baptismal sin can be forgiven *once* through repentance, but serial repentance is worthless.

The phrase "descended into the water" (*katabantes eis to hydōr*) confirms baptism by immersion as the referent. The Shepherd's claim to have been given *authority over repentance* (*edothē moi hē exousia*) is a remarkable claim to prophetic-apostolic authority.

EMET's "come to life" and LOGOS's "given new life" both render *ezēsa* (I lived/came alive). SOPHIA retains "I have come to life" — the aoristic past captures the sudden revivification Hermas describes.

---

## Mandate 6, Part 2 — On Repentance After Baptism

**40:1** "Lord," I said, "I wish to ask you one further matter." "Speak," he said. "Lord," I said, "I have heard from certain teachers that there is no repentance beyond the one we received when we descended into the water and obtained forgiveness of the sins we had previously committed."

**40:2** He said to me: "You have heard correctly, for so it stands. For one who has received forgiveness of sins ought never again to sin, but to abide in purity. Yet since you inquire precisely into all things, I will explain this as well — so as to give no excuse to those who will believe or to those who have already believed in the Lord. For those who have already believed or shall believe hereafter have no further repentance of sins, but they do have forgiveness of the sins they previously committed."

**40:3** "For those who were called before these days, the Lord appointed repentance. For the Lord, who searches the heart and foreknows all things, knew the weakness of human beings and the many devices of the devil, that he would work harm against the servants of God and do wickedness against them. Therefore, being compassionate, the Lord had mercy on his creation and established this repentance, and authority over this repentance was given to me."

**40:4** "But I tell you," he said, "if after that great and solemn calling anyone, being tempted by the devil, sins, he has one repentance. But if he sins and repents repeatedly, it profits such a man nothing — for with difficulty shall he live."

**40:5** I said to him: "I have come to life upon hearing these things from you so precisely. For I know that if I add no more to my sins, I shall be saved." "You shall be saved," he said, "you and all who do these things."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
